# Wordcell

> Wordcell keeps decisions, plans, and sources as Markdown beside your code,
> so coding agents can find them from the file they are about to change.

A new coding-agent session can read your code, but not the decisions that
stayed in the last session's chat. Wordcell keeps those decisions as Markdown
files beside the repository, with the plans that depend on them and the web
pages and PDFs that informed them. Tie a note to the paths it explains, and an
agent about to change that code runs one command to get the notes and plans
for that path. Exact search, backlinks, and Git history run on your machine
with no account or model, and every index rebuilds from files you can read in
any editor. Wordcell is free and open source.

When to use this site:
- Use wordcell.io to learn what Wordcell does, what stays on your machine, and
  the current install command.
- Use /developers for the coding-agent workflow: context for a repository path,
  AGENTS.md rules, Git history, and the Agent Skill.
- Use /docs for the documentation: a tutorial, how-to guides, the command
  reference, and design explanations.
- Use /blog for longer posts on why Wordcell works the way it does.

## Pages

- [Wordcell](https://wordcell.io/): Quick start, connecting a local agent, how
  notes, links, and search work, how Wordcell uses Oh, comparisons, publishing selected
  notes, what stays local, and the install command.
- [For developers](https://wordcell.io/developers): The coding-agent workflow:
  code-path context, scoped rules, note history, and the Agent Skill.
- [Benchmarks](https://wordcell.io/benchmarks): Wordcell exact search and optional
  reranking on 300 SciFact queries, with methods and raw results; separate
  sourced memory-retrieval studies from Oh and other systems.
- [Wordcell vs Basic Memory: two Markdown knowledge graphs](https://wordcell.io/compare/basic-memory):
  Where notes live, how notes form, note structure, search, repository
  context, and cost, with Basic Memory's documentation checked on
  September 26, 2026.
- [Wordcell vs Mem0: agent notes or per-user app memory](https://wordcell.io/compare/mem0): Where memory
  lives, how memories form, whose memory it is, the Platform and open-source
  split, and cost, with Mem0's documentation checked on September 26, 2026.
- [Wordcell vs Obsidian](https://wordcell.io/compare/obsidian): Coding-agent
  context and typed relationships alongside Obsidian’s editor, CLI, and Publish.
- [Wordcell vs Supermemory: files or a hosted memory API](https://wordcell.io/compare/supermemory):
  Where memory lives, how memories form, cost with Supermemory's pricing
  checked on September 26, 2026, connectors, compliance, agent access, and
  when to choose each.
- [Wordcell vs Claude-Mem: notes in Git or captured sessions](https://wordcell.io/compare/claude-mem):
  How memory forms, what loads at session start, where it is stored, what a
  fresh clone gets, and model use, with Claude-Mem 13.30.0 and its
  documentation checked on October 4, 2026.
- [Migrate from Supermemory to Wordcell](https://wordcell.io/migrate/supermemory):
  The install, export, import, and verify steps from the migration guide, with
  a prompt that connects a local agent.
- [Documentation](https://wordcell.io/docs): The documentation index, grouped
  into tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation, with the install
  command.
- [Get started](https://wordcell.io/docs/getting-started): The first-vault
  tutorial.
- [Overview](https://wordcell.io/docs/overview): What Wordcell does, how to
  install it, and how a coding agent uses a vault, on one page.
- [Use Wordcell with a coding agent](https://wordcell.io/docs/agent-workflow):
  Set up, query, maintain, and revise repository memory.
- [Connect Wordcell to your coding agent](https://wordcell.io/docs/agent-handoffs):
  Register the local MCP server with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Claude
  Desktop, check that the agent reads your notes, and fix common errors.
- [Use Wordcell with an existing Obsidian vault](https://wordcell.io/docs/obsidian):
  Which Obsidian links, tags, and attachments Wordcell reads, and how to serve
  a vault to a coding agent without changing it.
- [Reference](https://wordcell.io/docs/reference): Exact commands, formats,
  SDK imports, optional adapters, and the local MCP server (wordcell mcp)
  with its flags and tools.
- [Publish](https://wordcell.io/docs/publish): Select notes and build a static
  site.
- [Migrate from Supermemory](https://wordcell.io/docs/migration-from-supermemory):
  Export Supermemory documents and memory entries, import them as Markdown
  notes, and see what does not transfer.
- [Sync a vault with Git](https://wordcell.io/docs/sync): Keep one vault
  current on several machines with a private repository and a scheduled
  commit and push.
- [Comparisons](https://wordcell.io/docs/comparisons): Markdown tools such as
  QMD, Basic Memory, and Obsidian, Claude Code's built-in memory and
  claude-mem, and agent memory services such as Supermemory, Mem0, and Zep,
  compared with Wordcell from primary sources.
- [Evidence](https://wordcell.io/docs/evidence): The reproducible
  development fixtures used to check passage selection and context size, with
  their raw reports; source-ranking benchmarks are on /benchmarks.
- [Markdown-memory retrieval pilot](https://wordcell.io/docs/markdown-memory-pilot): Historical measurements and methods on a frozen repository corpus.

## Blog

- [Wordcell blog](https://wordcell.io/blog): Posts on how Wordcell keeps
  Markdown as the record and how it works with other Hraness tools. Atom feed:
  https://wordcell.io/blog/feed.xml
- [The marked region: managed and authored vaults](https://wordcell.io/blog/managed-or-authored):
  The one marked block a tool may rewrite, the authored-vault option, and why
  malformed markers fail closed.
- [Free local agent memory in Markdown files you own](https://wordcell.io/blog/free-local-agent-memory):
  What the launch adds, the measured results with their limits, and how to
  move from Supermemory.
- [Introducing Wordcell](https://wordcell.io/blog/introducing-wordcell): Who
  Wordcell suits, one saved rule traced to a cited search and graph answer,
  and its limits.
- [How Wordcell uses Oh](https://wordcell.io/blog/how-wordcell-uses-oh): How
  a graph answer carries a proof back to the Markdown files that support it.
